utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: Hi Leila. How are things at home this week?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: My stepdad has been hitting me again. It happens when my mom is at work. He says if I tell anyone he'll make things worse.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: That sounds like a very difficult home environment. How long has this tension with your stepfather been going on?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Since he moved in two years ago. Last week was the worst. He hit me hard enough that I had a bruise on my arm for five days. My kid is being hurt too — he grabbed her arm and shook her.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: Physical conflict in the home can create a very unsafe environment for children. Have you considered talking to your mother about setting clearer boundaries with your stepfather?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: My mom doesn't believe me. She thinks I'm exaggerating. It's not just me — he beats me regularly and the kids see it. My daughter is terrified of him.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: It's very painful when those closest to us don't validate our experiences. That lack of support compounds the stress. Let's talk about how you can build resilience in that environment.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: I don't need resilience, I need help. Is there anything you can actually do? I'm scared for my daughter.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: I understand you're scared. Let's explore your support network and look at some resources that might be helpful.
